object_description: Angled group of independent school and sports hall volumes
design_condition: The buildings are precisely aligned with the adjacent industrial hall while grouping around a playground and grass field, with entrances and break areas set back from traffic and the sports hall independently connected to parking.

positive.statement: The buildings form a spacious and convincing overall complex in relation to the residential development.
The outdoor spaces have beautiful spatial relationships and high quality in use and access.
The entrances and break areas are set back from traffic and protected.
The sports hall is functionally well connected to parking and can operate completely separately from school operations.
The clear building structure enables a high degree of flexibility in classroom layout and allocation.
The central access zone with opposing cascade staircases is spatially attractive.
The project has a relatively cheap building volume and below-average expected investment and management costs.
The balanced ratio of window to wall areas is particularly noticeable in sustainability terms.

negative.statement: The outdoor design is somewhat schematic in its implementation.
The limited distance from the eastern industrial area is expected to cause disruptions to school operations.
The integration of ball-stopping fences is spatially problematic and may disrupt school operations.
The ground-floor layout, sanitary rooms and escape stairs raise structural and organizational questions.
The kindergarten cloakroom corridor appears problematic because it is illuminated only through the kindergarten rooms.
The auditorium and adjoining rooms would have to be optimized.
The sanitary rooms are confusingly arranged and far too small.
The sports hall adjoining rooms require more operationally balanced allocation across the floors.
The facades remain schematic and lack the public character of a school and sports facility.
The materialization should be differentiated more carefully inside and outside to support the atmosphere of a primary school building.
The widely projecting upper floors are complex and contradict the more vertical structure.
The fire-protection solutions should be questioned regarding the effort involved.
